articles.title: Syrian Arab Republic: Population Mobility and Baseline Assessment — Round 20 (01–30 September 2026)
articles.description: Please refer to the attached file. Since the transition of power on 8 December 2024, the Syrian Arab Republic (hereafter referred to as Syria) has experienced substantial shifts in its humanitarian, political, and demographic landscape. Population movements remain dynamic, with returns recorded across all 14 governorates alongside continued displacement. While changing security conditions have influenced mobility patterns, persistent gaps in housing, livelihoods, and access to essential services continue to affect the ability of returnees to re-establish their lives and sustain their return. The escalation of hostilities across the Middle East since 28 February 2026 has further influenced displacement dynamics, contributing to continued cross-border movements. This report presents mobility trends recorded during September 2026 by the International Organization Migration's (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), together with updated baseline estimates for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), IDP returnees within Syria, and arrivals from abroad, including both those returning to their areas of origin and those settling elsewhere. This report should be read alongside Communities of Return Index Round 5 for additional context. The findings in this report provide an evidence base to support humanitarian response, early recovery programming and planning for durable solutions.
